report.tagline: A design tool that runs in the browser where a whole team can design, prototype, and now build apps and websites together at the same time.
report.simpleSummary: Figma is like Google Docs for designing apps and websites. Designers draw screens, and engineers, product managers and marketers can open the same file in a browser link and comment or copy code. Many people can work in one file at once, and you see their cursors move. Since 2025 it also has AI tools that turn a written idea into a working app, plus tools for websites, slides and marketing graphics.

overview.whatItDoes: Figma lets teams design screens for apps and websites, turn them into clickable prototypes, and hand them to engineers, all in a browser. FigJam is its online whiteboard for brainstorming. Since Config 2025 Figma has added Figma Make (AI that builds working apps from a prompt), Figma Sites (publish websites), Figma Slides (presentations), Figma Buzz (marketing graphics) and Figma Draw (illustration).
howItWorks: Open figma.com in a browser or the desktop app. Files live in the cloud, so there is nothing to email or save.
Share a link. Anyone can view; people with paid seats can edit at the same time, with live cursors.
Designers build reusable components and design systems, so a button changed once updates everywhere.
Dev Mode shows engineers exact sizes, colours and code snippets, and the MCP server lets AI coding tools read designs directly.
Figma Make and the Figma agent use AI credits to generate layouts, prototypes and working code from text prompts.
Companies pay per seat: Full seats for designers, Dev seats for engineers, Collab seats for everyone else.
overview.valueProposition: Everyone who touches a product (design, engineering, product, marketing) works from one live file instead of passing around screenshots and old versions, so products ship faster with fewer mistakes.

painPoints.pain: Design files emailed back and forth, with nobody sure which version is final.
painPoints.howSolved: One cloud file with a link. Everyone sees the latest version and version history.

painPoints.pain: Designers and engineers misread each other, so the built app looks different from the design.
painPoints.howSolved: Dev Mode, code snippets and the MCP server give engineers and AI coding tools the exact specs.

painPoints.pain: Feedback comes late and scattered across chat and email.
painPoints.howSolved: Comments sit right on the design, and stakeholders join with a free or low-cost seat.

painPoints.pain: Keeping buttons, colours and fonts consistent across a big product.
painPoints.howSolved: Components, variables and shared libraries update every file when the source changes.

painPoints.pain: Turning an idea into something clickable takes days.
painPoints.howSolved: Prototyping links screens in minutes, and Figma Make can build a working app from a prompt.

painPoints.pain: Old design tools only worked on Mac and needed installs.
painPoints.howSolved: Runs in any browser on Mac, Windows or Linux.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Many people edit one file at once with live cursors, comments and audio chat.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The original reason Figma beat Sketch. It turns design from a solo task into a team activity, which brings in non-designers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Reusable parts and shared libraries with variables for colour, spacing and modes like dark mode.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Big companies build their whole design system in Figma, which makes it very hard to leave.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Gives engineers specs and code, and lets AI coding tools like Cursor and Claude Code read and write designs.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Brings engineers in as paying users and keeps Figma at the centre as coding moves to AI tools. MCP usage grew 3x in Q3 2026.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Type a prompt or paste a design and get a working, clickable app with real code.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Figma's answer to AI app builders like Lovable and v0. Lets PMs and founders build without a designer, and drives AI credit revenue.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Online whiteboard for brainstorms, flowcharts and retros, also usable from ChatGPT.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Cheap way to bring PMs, engineers and other teams into Figma, who may later use design files.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Publish websites, make presentations and create on-brand marketing graphics from the same design system.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Expands Figma from product design into marketing and communication, a much bigger group of users.

businessModel.summary: Figma sells monthly seats. Companies pay for each designer, engineer and collaborator, with higher prices on bigger plans. Large companies keep adding seats and plans, so revenue from existing customers grows about 31% a year. AI credits are now a second way to earn more from the same customers.

revenueStreams.detail: For designers and heavy users. Access to Figma Design, Make, Sites, Slides, Buzz and Draw. Biggest revenue source.
For engineers who inspect designs and use Dev Mode and the MCP server.
Low-cost seats for PMs, marketers and others who use FigJam and Slides or comment.
Higher per-seat prices for admin controls, security and shared design systems across many teams.
Each seat includes some AI credits; heavy users buy more. Over 80% of $10K+ customers now consume credits.

businessModel.pricing: Free Starter plan with limits. Professional: Full seat about $16 per month billed yearly ($20 monthly), Dev seat about $12, Collab seat about $3. Organization: Full seat about $55 per month, yearly only. Enterprise: Full seat about $90 per month, yearly only. Extra AI credits are sold on top. Prices from the March 2025 seat change; check the site for current figures.
costDrivers: Engineering and research staff, including stock-based pay
Cloud hosting for real-time editing of very large files
AI model costs for Make, the agent and other AI features
Sales teams for large enterprise deals
Events like Config and community programs
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a mid-size company with 50 designers on Organization Full seats at $55, 150 engineers on Dev seats at about $25, and 300 Collab seats at about $5. That is about $2,750 + $3,750 + $1,500 = $8,000 a month, or roughly $96,000 a year. Figma keeps about 80% after hosting and AI costs, based on its 80% gross margin. Because the same company adds seats and AI credits each year, a $96,000 customer today often pays about $125,000 next year (131% net dollar retention). Seat mix figures are an illustration.

howTheyGetUsers: Free plan for individuals and students, so designers learn Figma first
Shared links: every designer sends files to PMs, engineers and clients, who see Figma without installing anything
Community: free files, plugins and UI kits shared by designers
Config conference and launches that get wide press
New products (Make, Sites, Slides, Buzz) bring in non-designers
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily design work lives in Figma files
Company design systems and libraries are stored there
Comments and review requests pull people in
AI coding tools read Figma through the MCP server, so designs stay the source of truth
growth.moat: Figma's moat is that the whole team works in it, not just designers. A company's design system, years of files and every engineer's workflow depend on it. Switching would mean moving thousands of components and retraining hundreds of people. Being the standard also means new designers learn Figma first.

competitors.name: Adobe (XD, Photoshop, Illustrator, Express)
competitors.positioning: Long-time leader in creative software. Tried to buy Figma for $20B, but the deal was dropped in 2023 under regulator pressure.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Figma is browser-first and built for teams working together. Adobe is stronger for photo, video and illustration.

competitors.name: Canva
competitors.positioning: Easy design for non-designers: social posts, slides, docs.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Figma is deeper for product design and dev handoff. Canva is easier for marketing and wins on reach. Figma Buzz and Slides now compete directly.

competitors.name: AI app builders (Lovable, v0, Bolt)
competitors.positioning: Type a prompt, get a working web app with code.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Figma Make uses your real design system and sits next to the design files. Pure AI builders are faster for coders who skip design.

competitors.name: Framer and Webflow
competitors.positioning: Design and publish websites without code.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Figma Sites is newer. Framer and Webflow have more mature publishing, hosting and CMS features.

competitors.name: Sketch and Penpot
competitors.positioning: Sketch is a Mac-only design app; Penpot is free and open source.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Figma has the real-time teamwork and network of users that these lack.

northStar.metric: Weekly active editors across all Figma products (people who create or change something in a file each week)
northStar.why: Figma is worth more when more people from more roles do real work in it. Viewers matter less than people editing, prototyping, building with Make or writing code from designs. More weekly editors means more seats and more AI use.

improvementIdeas.problem: Designs drift away from what is really built, so files go stale.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Through the MCP server, pull real components from code back into Figma so design and code match. Keeps Figma as the source of truth even as AI writes more code.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of libraries linked to a code repo; weekly MCP write-back users

improvementIdeas.idea: Clear seat and credit dashboard for admins
improvementIdeas.problem: Admins are confused by seat types and AI credit use.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: One page showing who uses what, unused seats and credit forecasts. Fewer surprise bills and fewer angry downgrades.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Billing support tickets; seat churn after renewal

improvementIdeas.problem: AI-built prototypes look generic and do not use the company's design system.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Force Make to build only from the company library by default. Output is usable, so more of it is shared and shipped.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Share of Make prototypes shared or moved into design files

improvementIdeas.problem: Big enterprise files lag and crash.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Load only visible pages and lighter previews. Fewer complaints from the most valuable customers.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: P95 file load time; crash rate on files over 500MB

improvementIdeas.problem: Many new designers in markets like India use free plans and switch to cheaper tools.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Local currency pricing and student-to-pro discounts. Builds future enterprise users.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Paid seat growth in India; student-to-paid conversion

pmLessons: Make the product better with more people. Multiplayer made each new teammate a reason to stay.
Free viewers are the best sales team. Engineers and PMs who opened a link became paying users later.
Expanding to new products works best when it reuses what you already own. Sites, Slides and Buzz all use the same design system.
Seat pricing changes are risky. Even good changes upset users if they are hard to understand.
When AI threatens your core user, put AI inside your product and connect it to where work goes next, like Figma did with Make and MCP.

interviewQuestions.question: AI coding tools can turn a prompt into a working app. Is Figma at risk? What would you do as a PM?
interviewQuestions.hint: Name the threat: fewer design files needed. Then Figma's assets: design systems, team review, brand control. Ideas: MCP, Make, code sync. Pick one metric like weekly MCP users.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of Figma Make?
interviewQuestions.hint: Go beyond prompts sent. Use: prototypes shared, prototypes turned into real designs or code, repeat use after 30 days. Guardrails: AI cost per user and complaint rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Figma Slides competes with Google Slides and PowerPoint. Who should it target first?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick a niche where Figma wins: design and product teams who already have brand assets in Figma. Explain why broad users are hard. Define one adoption metric.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain Figma's 131% net dollar retention to a non-business person, and how you would grow it.
interviewQuestions.hint: Customers spend 31% more each year. Growth paths: more seats, higher plans, AI credits, new products. Pick one and size it.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature that brings more engineers into Figma every day.
interviewQuestions.hint: Start from engineer pain: specs, changes, code. Ideas: change alerts in GitHub, design diffs, MCP inside IDEs. Metric: weekly active Dev seats.
